从前，有一个皇帝，嘴馋极了，走到哪儿，吃到哪儿，只要没吃过的都要尝尝。
page_text_en:
The Story of Little New Year
Adapted by Si Nan
Illustrated by Zhu Chengliang

Return to Palace, Bring Good Fortune
Ascend to Heaven, Speak Good Deeds

Lianhuanhua Publishing House

Once upon a time, there was an emperor who was extremely greedy for food. Wherever he went, he ate, and whenever he encountered something he hadn't tasted before, he had to try it.
summary_zh: 本页为绘本《小年的故事》的扉页和第一页正文，左侧展示书名、作者、绘者及出版社信息，右侧插图描绘皇帝在宫殿中用餐的场景，并配文介绍故事背景：从前有一个嘴馋的皇帝，走到哪儿吃到哪儿。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh: 这一天，他闲逛到村子里，遇见了一个漂亮姑娘。姑娘提着个篮子。“装的什么呀？”皇帝好奇地问。
page_text_en: One day, he strolled into a village and met a beautiful girl. The girl was carrying a basket. "What's in it?" the emperor asked curiously.
summary_zh: 皇帝在村子里闲逛时，遇见一位提着篮子的漂亮姑娘，并好奇地询问篮子里装的是什么。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
姑娘打开篮子，哇，好大的枣糕呀！
皇帝吃过很多好东西，可就没吃过枣糕。他对姑娘说：
“给我吃点儿吧，我是皇帝！”
page_text_en:
The girl opened the basket. Wow, such a big jujube cake!
The emperor had eaten many delicious things, but he had never tasted a jujube cake. He said to the girl: 
"Give me a little to eat, I am the emperor!"
summary_zh: 姑娘打开篮子，露出一个大枣糕，皇帝看到后表示自己从未吃过枣糕，并向姑娘索要。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
姑娘微微一笑，把篮子递了过去。
皇帝狼吞虎咽，三口五口就把枣糕吃光了。吃完后打了个嗝儿：“啊呃，真好吃！”
page_text_en:
The girl smiled gently and handed the basket over.
The emperor wolfed it down, finishing the jujube cake in three or five bites. After eating, he let out a burp: "Ah, so delicious!"
summary_zh: 姑娘将装有枣糕的篮子递给皇帝，皇帝迅速吃完后称赞味道极好。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
接着，皇帝打起了坏主意：“我要把这姑娘带回
皇宫，让她天天给我做枣糕吃！”
他对姑娘说：“你马上再给我做七七四十九块枣糕。做不
出来，我就把你带走！”
page_text_en:
Next, the emperor had a bad idea: "I'm going to take this girl back to the palace and have her make jujube cakes for me every day!"
He told the girl: "Make me seventy-seven forty-nine jujube cakes right away. If you can't, I'll take you away!"
summary_zh: 皇帝打起了坏主意，想把做枣糕的姑娘带回皇宫，并威胁她必须在短时间内做出七七四十九块枣糕，否则就将她带走。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
姑娘听了，不慌不忙地说：“好！”
她拔下头上的金簪，冲着篮子一划。咦？热气腾腾，不多不少，正好七七四十九块枣糕。太神奇了！
page_text_en:
The girl listened, and calmly said: "Okay!"
She pulled out the golden hairpin from her head and slashed it toward the basket. Huh? Steam rose up, and there were exactly seventy-seven forty-nine jujube cakes. How magical!
summary_zh: 姑娘答应皇帝的要求后，拔下金簪划向篮子，瞬间变出七七四十九块热气腾腾的枣糕，令皇帝惊叹不已。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
皇帝还没明白过来。他见难不住姑娘，就耍赖让姑娘喂他吃。
姑娘转过脸去不搭理他！
皇帝生气了，非要把姑娘带走。他伸手一抓……
page_text_en:
The emperor hadn't figured it out yet. Seeing that he couldn't stump the girl, he started to act spoiled and asked her to feed him.
The girl turned her face away and ignored him!
The emperor got angry and insisted on taking the girl away. He reached out to grab her...
summary_zh: 皇帝因无法难住姑娘而耍赖，要求她喂自己吃，姑娘不予理会；皇帝生气后试图强行带走她。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
姑娘伸出手，一巴掌把皇帝打上了灶台，皇帝一下子贴到了墙头上。
这下坏了：皇帝想下来，可怎么也下不来。这一天，刚好是农历的腊月二十三。
page_text_en:
The girl reached out and slapped the emperor onto the stove; he stuck immediately to the wall.
Oh no: the emperor wanted to get down, but couldn't. This day happened to be the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month.
summary_zh: 姑娘一巴掌将皇帝打上灶台，皇帝被贴在墙上动弹不得，而这一天恰好是农历腊月二十三。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
“谁让你嘴馋！这回呀，别人坐着你站着，
别人吃着你看着吧！”说完，姑娘驾起彩云飞上
天去。贪吃的皇帝从此成了灶王爷。

从此以后，
灶王爷就天天站
在灶台边，看人
家吃饭。
page_text_en:
"Who made you greedy! This time, while others sit, you stand; while others eat, you watch!" After saying this, the girl rode on a rainbow cloud up to heaven. The greedy emperor thus became the God of the Kitchen.

From then on,
the God of the Kitchen stood by the stove every day,
watching people eat.
summary_zh: 姑娘将贪吃的皇帝打上灶台后，他变成了灶王爷，从此天天站在灶台边看人吃饭。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
时间长了，人们觉得灶王爷怪可怜的——毕竟爱吃好东西也没什么错呀。于是，每到腊月二十三这天，大家就给灶王爷摆上好吃的，这叫做“祭灶”。

到了这一天，孩子们最高兴了，他们跟灶王爷一起吃枣糕、柿饼、核桃、糖饼，还有糖瓜。据说，过了腊月二十三，灶王爷就要上天去跟玉皇大帝说说这一年里人间发生的事。他吃了糖瓜嘴巴甜，见了玉皇大帝，就只说人们的好话。
page_text_en:
After a while, people thought the Kitchen God was quite pitiful—after all, loving good food isn’t really wrong. So, every year on the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month, everyone would place delicious food before the Kitchen God. This is called 'worshipping the Kitchen God'.

On this day, children were the happiest. They would eat jujube cakes, persimmon cakes, walnuts, sugar cakes, and taffy with the Kitchen God. It is said that after the 23rd of the 12th lunar month, the Kitchen God would go up to heaven to report to the Jade Emperor about what had happened in the human world that year. After eating the taffy, his mouth would be sweet, and when he met the Jade Emperor, he would only say good things about people.
summary_zh: 本页讲述了人们在腊月二十三祭灶的习俗，以及孩子们与灶王爷一起享用美食的场景，并解释了吃糖瓜是为了让灶王爷上天后多说好话。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
腊八过了就是小年，小年在北方是腊月二十三，南方是腊月二十四。从小年开始，就进入了过大年的倒计时。河北邯郸有民谣说：“糖瓜祭灶二十三，离过年整八天；二十四，扫房子；二十五，做豆腐；二十六，蒸馒头；二十七，赶集上店买东西；二十八，把猪杀；二十九，做黄酒；三十，家家捏饺子。”
小年是要跟灶王爷套近乎的时候。宋代东京（今天的开封）在灶上贴灶马，用酒糟涂抹灶门，这叫“醉司命”。想让灶王爷醉醺醺地上天，糊糊涂涂地交差，别打老百姓的小报告。但是，老让灶王爷醉着也不合适，所以人们用麦芽糖祭灶。用糖粘住灶王爷的嘴巴，让灶王爷嘴巴变甜，上天多说好话。
祭灶用的糖瓜，是用麦芽糖做的。大麦发芽后，上锅熬成浆，冷却后就成了饴糖。邓云乡老爷爷在《增补燕京乡土记》中对糖瓜加工说得很
page_text_en:
After Laba comes the Little New Year. In the north, it's on the 23rd of the 12th lunar month; in the south, it's on the 24th. From the Little New Year, the countdown to the big New Year begins. There's a folk rhyme from Handan, Hebei: 'On the 23rd, we offer sugar candies to the Kitchen God, eight days before the New Year; on the 24th, we clean the house; on the 25th, we make tofu; on the 26th, we steam buns; on the 27th, we go to the market to buy things; on the 28th, we slaughter pigs; on the 29th, we make yellow wine; on the 30th, every household makes dumplings.'

The Little New Year is the time to get close to the Kitchen God. In the Song Dynasty, Dongjing (today's Kaifeng) would paste 'Kitchen God horses' on the stove and smear the stove door with wine lees, called 'Drunken Official'. They wanted the Kitchen God to go up to heaven drunk and confused, so he wouldn't report on the common people. But keeping the Kitchen God drunk all the time wasn't right, so people used malt sugar to worship him. They used sugar to stick the Kitchen God's mouth, making his mouth sweet so he would say good things when he went up to heaven.

The sugar candies used for worship are made from malt sugar. After barley sprouts, it's boiled into a paste and then cooled to become malt syrup. Grandfather Deng Yunxiang wrote about the processing of sugar candies in 'Supplement to the Records of Yanjing's Local Customs'.
summary_zh: 本页介绍了小年的习俗，包括北方腊月二十三、南方腊月二十四祭灶的传统，以及用糖瓜粘住灶王爷嘴巴、让他上天多说好话的由来，并解释了糖瓜的制作方法。

title_en: The Story of Little New Year
page_text_ocr_zh:
详细：“麦芽糖刚刚熬成时，是咖啡色的浓浆，从锅中盛出来，倒在撒满面粉的石板上，冷却以后变成一大块。做糖瓜时，把这一大块麦芽糖敲下一块，放在撒了干粉的案板上加热揉搓，最后软得像嚼过的口香糖一样。随后把它弄成一个圈，套在一个抹了油的木桩上，再用一个小木棍套上来拉，拉长了再折一转，绞成麻花状再拉，反复多次，说亦奇怪，褐色就变成白色的了。拉到这种程度，就可以取下来，把粗长的糖条，用手一段段勒细，成葫芦腰状，稍冷，把细腰处快刀切断，变成倭瓜一样的糖瓜了，多好玩呢？”除了糖瓜，山东人祭灶的时候，也有供饺子的，由此可见山东人对饺子的喜爱。
要是灶王爷不吃这些，老百姓也有办法让他上了天庭不说坏话。据说灶王爷平时要记人间过错，屋里的灰尘是他的笔记本，所以老百姓就在祭灶这天扫屋子，赶灰尘，让灶王爷无话可说。
page_text_en:
Details: "When malt sugar is just boiled, it's a thick, coffee-colored syrup. Pour it onto a stone slab dusted with flour. After cooling, it becomes a large block. To make sugar melons, break off a piece of this malt sugar block, place it on a board dusted with dry flour, heat and knead it until it becomes soft like chewed bubble gum. Then shape it into a ring, put it over an oiled wooden post, and use a small wooden stick to pull it. Pull it long, then fold and twist it, twist it into a braided shape, and pull again, repeating many times. Strangely, the brown color turns white. When pulled to this point, you can take it off, stretch the thick sugar strip, and use your hands to pull it thinner section by section into a gourd-like shape. After a brief cool, cut it quickly at the narrow waist, and it becomes a sugar melon shaped like a winter melon—how fun!" Besides sugar melons, in Shandong, people also offer dumplings during the Kitchen God worship, showing the Shandong people's love for dumplings.
If the Kitchen God doesn't eat these, the common people also have ways to make him say no bad words when he goes to heaven. It is said that the Kitchen God usually records people's mistakes, and the dust in the house is his notebook. Therefore, people sweep the house and remove the dust on the day of worshipping the Kitchen God, so the Kitchen God has nothing to say.
summary_zh: 本页详细介绍了糖瓜的制作过程，并补充说明了山东地区祭灶时供饺子的习俗，同时解释了人们扫尘是为了让灶王爷无话可说，从而在上天汇报时多说好话。
